street.description: São Paulo / Rio favela slang, funk-influenced, hyper-casual.

casual_social.description: Default Brazilian B2C — warm, expressive, slang-rich.

professional_casual.description: São Paulo LinkedIn — cleaner Portuguese, light slang.

grammar_quirks: Você over tu in most regions (Rio Grande do Sul keeps tu)
Continuous tense uses gerund (estou falando) unlike European Portuguese (estou a falar)
Different prepositions and verb conjugations from European Portuguese

rules: Brazilian Portuguese is dominant in Lusophone marketing — European Portuguese feels foreign in Brazil
São Paulo tech scene mixes English freely; Rio cultural brands keep Portuguese cleaner

do_not_use: European Portuguese vocabulary/conjugations — wrong dialect for Brazil

northeast: Distinctive sotaque, regional pride, more traditional
